name: United Kingdom
tagline: The system built for the IB, at the price of leaving the EU
summary: UK admissions are built around the fact that applicants do not yet have their results. Universities make conditional offers expressed in IB points — "36 overall including 6,6,5 at Higher Level" — and confirm them in July when the results arrive. For an IB student that solves an awkward problem: you know the exact grades you need before you sit the exams. What it introduced instead is cost: since Brexit an EU citizen pays the international fee, and there is no EU rate to fall back on.
whyConsider: Conditional offers in IB points solve the July problem outright: the whole process is designed around results that have not arrived yet.
One application, five choices, one personal statement, one reference — for almost every undergraduate course in the country.
Three-year bachelor degrees in England, Wales and Northern Ireland, so the total cost of a degree is less lopsided against the annual fee than it first looks.
watchOuts: An EU citizen pays the international fee. There is no EU rate, no home-fee status and, for most students, no access to UK student loans. This is the thing that decides whether the UK is realistic.
Oxford, Cambridge, medicine, dentistry and veterinary medicine all close on 15 October 2026 — more than a year before the course starts, and before most students have thought about applying at all.
Admissions tests for those courses register earlier still, and the registration deadline is not the test date.
Scotland runs four-year degrees and a separate system; Wales and Northern Ireland differ again on fees and support. "The UK" is four systems sharing one application portal.

ibRecognition.minimumPoints: No national minimum. Offers are made per course in IB points and usually name Higher Level subject grades as well — 36 points including 6,6,5 at HL is a typical competitive offer, and the range across the sector is wide.
ibRecognition.subjectLevelRule: Set per course and normally expressed as HL subject grades rather than as a national rule. Where a subject is essential it is named, and it is almost always required at Higher Level.

language.englishProof: Set per university. An IB Diploma taught in English, or IB English A or B at a stated grade, is normally accepted in place of a test. Confirm with the university, because visa rules and university rules are not the same rules.

feeContext.summary: Since Brexit, EU, EEA and Swiss citizens pay the international fee, the same as any other overseas applicant. It is set per university and subject: at Glasgow, for example, GBP 28,275 a year for arts and social sciences and GBP 33,708 for science and engineering in 2027/28.

sectorLandscape.summary: Almost every UK undergraduate course, at almost every institution, is applied for through one portal — which makes the sector look more uniform than it is. Underneath sit universities of very different ages and purposes, specialist conservatoires and art schools, further education colleges teaching degrees under a university’s validation, and degree apprenticeships that are jobs first. And the UK is four education systems, not one: Scotland’s degrees are four years and its fee and qualification rules are its own.

routes.what: Three-year bachelor degrees in England, Wales and Northern Ireland, four in Scotland, and specialised from the first term — you apply to read a subject rather than to a college in general. That suits a student who already knows, and suits a student who does not rather less than the Scottish or Dutch alternatives.

A separate system inside the same portal. Four-year honours degrees with a broader first two years, closer to a liberal-arts structure, and distinct fee and funding rules. For a student who wants to keep options open a while longer, this is the UK route to look at.
Music, dance and drama, with their own application route (UCAS Conservatoires) and their own calendar. Admission is by audition, and grades matter far less than the audition does.
routes.note: Applied for separately from the main UCAS scheme. Not covered in detail on this site.

routes.what: A paid job with a degree attached, funded by the employer, with no tuition fee to the apprentice. Applied for through the employer rather than UCAS, on the employer’s timetable.
routes.note: Almost always restricted to UK residents, so rarely open to an applicant from Denmark.

notes: Re-check before 15 October 2026, which is the first deadline that can cost a student the year.

Not established: a sector-wide tuition figure, which varies by university and subject (Glasgow 2027/28 is recorded as an example); and admissions-test dates, which are set by the test providers rather than by UCAS (they are on the country profile).
